reviews.title: Dangerous app
reviews.text: App regularly copies your clipboard for no reason; it was great that IOS now tells you that this is occurring.  Whatever you  copied last on your phone becomes the knowledge of Alibaba (passwords, personal notes that you were working on, etc.)  There’s no reason for this to occur other than fishing for information.   Just use the website.   Additional note: once you have an account, you will receive emails showing you items for a low price, but when you go to the site, you can’t get it for that price.  Example: video projector for $9.43 (picture shows the projector, and only the projector).   Click on the link, log in, and it turns out that the price is for the stand for the projector, but the projector is actually $68.   If the price looks low in the email, they’re scamming you.    However, I’ve had decent success with electronic parts and with customer service.  Not great, but not horrible either.

reviews.title: Preferable to website despite odd choices
reviews.text:
The app seems to be a dedicated browser for Alis website (presumably so you can’t deselect tracking cookies), so it shares some of the websites odd choices: After some time, you cannot review products (so a lot of the reviews are “received product, it looks like the picture, but I haven’t tried it”).  Currency switches to USD in some displays, even if that’s not your chosen currency.  If you view a product once, you’re bombarded with identical products from other sellers going forward, it’ll take weeks of browsing to flush it out of your profile (“The Grimace” allows you to remove things from your profile, say, if you bought it as a gift).   The app, however, will let you stay logged in longer, to avoid Alis awkward login process.
Where the app is actually worse than the website (other than possibly tracking) is sound feedback: you cannot mute it (iOS should really allow that, but doesn’t), so the idiotic candy-crush’esque jingle when collecting “coins” will forever annoy you.   It still seems to have a complicated relationship with on-device storage (though you can now clear the cache, hurrah): despite Apple claiming it is a 91MB app, my iPad says it occupies ca 700MB (after clearing cache).  After most recent upgrade, it decided that “for you” items should be jewelry, fake eyebrows and trinkets, something I have never looked at before.  Sadly, there seems to be no way to stop that, other than actively browsing other products, so that’s quite sinister.  The quality of the pr

reviews.title: AliExpress: A nightmare on Elm Street
reviews.text: I was an Elite customer who had spent thousands on AliExpress. Three returns completely changed my view of the platform… First, a damaged car window visor arrived. I paid the return postage myself, but instead of reimbursing me, AliExpress eventually offered a coupon… Second, I received expensive car seat covers that looked nothing like the listing. I returned the heavy package to the address provided, with tracking showing delivery, yet my refund was rejected and even the promised return postage was not reimbursed… Third, after learning from those experiences, I refused to return another item until AliExpress confirmed in writing whether Australia Post was acceptable and whether the full postage would be reimbursed as money. Instead of answering a simple question, the case entered another confusing cycle while a countdown warned that I could lose my refund… Three returns, three exhausting disputes. My experience is that the real test of a shopping platform begins when something goes wrong. After this, I no longer trust AliExpress with my purchases.

reviews.title: Cheap, shameless, unreliable
reviews.text: It’s actually a really good app to use if you do NOT run into any issues, but if you do, it’s nightmare. Do not expect issues to be addressed or any sort of fairness/reasoning to be upheld. They outsource their app customer service team to cheap labour countries who first give you repetitive, sometimes nonsense template responses, waiting for you to get either too frustrated so you give up, or disconnected once you leave the app/conversation for too long. If that doesn’t work, it’ll tell you the case has been escalated to a higher team and some will get back to you via emails - those emails arrive fast enough, but they never, ever address anything. It’s again, template sometimes lengthy emails that literally repeat their ‘policies’ and regardless of what you reply or reply with - such as supporting evidence or documents - you will get yet another similar, or often identical response as if your previous reply never existed. Then you’d like to raise a complaint - great, it’s the same team handling complaints so you’ll yet again get the same responses, NOT EVEN with an acknowledgement that a compliant has been received. You get nowhere with them, but if you’re buying over £100 using a credit card you’ll at least have a chargeback option under the UK law. If not, you’re on your own. Best of luck using this app. Ps: Mr Jack Ma should feel really ashamed for this since China has been working so hard for its ‘reputation’!

They sent me a label for one and QR codes to have usps scan them for them to print the labels. I work nights so it took me a little while to get them to usps. I dropped the labeled package off and stupidly didn’t get a receipt. I went to check the tracking and usps didn’t recognize it. I tried to dispute it with aliexpress half a dozen times and they would ask for the label and then turn around and say it wasn’t enough proof. It was only $48 so you’d think they would just cover it considering how much I’ve spent over the years. Oh, and the two QR codes disappeared because I didn’t get them scanned quite fast enough so I’ll probably lose that money too. If you do use aliexpress then it’s a good idea to take a video of you opening the package and always get a receipt from usps if you do return it. I’m not sure in going to go through that trouble so I guess I just won’t use them anymore.

reviews.title: Impossible Navigation
reviews.text: Cluttered and Overwhelming UI: The app is a visual nightmare. From the moment you open it, you're bombarded with intrusive pop-ups, flashing ads, and "silly games" that feel more like a digital casino than a shop. Useless Search & Navigation: Finding specific items is nearly impossible. The search engine is "pointless," often ignoring filters or showing completely unrelated results to what you actually typed. Deceptive Pricing: Listed prices often change once you add an item to your cart, with hidden shipping fees suddenly making the "deal" much more expensive than local alternatives. The Customer Service Abyss: If anything goes wrong, you are stuck with automated bots that provide "copy and paste" responses. The dispute process is a frustrating multi-step ordeal where legitimate refund requests are often rejected despite clear evidence of wrong or missing items. Buggy Experience: The app frequently hangs, crashes, or fails to update order tracking, requiring constant restarts or re-installations just to function. Bottom Line: Unless you have hours to waste navigating a broken interface and fighting for a fiver refund, avoid this app and stick to more reliable platforms.

reviews.title: Scammers
reviews.text:
I am genuinely disappointed to have to leave a mixed review, as my experience with this app for regular purchases has been consistently five-star up until now. For months, placing orders was seamless, fast, and reliable. I often recommended the app to friends because the ordering process itself is so intuitive and the selection is fantastic.
The entire system worked flawlessly until I had an issue that required a refund. Unfortunately, despite following the outlined procedures and being promised a refund, the money was never returned to my account. I have reached out multiple times to customer support, and the lack of resolution or communication regarding the scam of the unfulfilled refund has been deeply concerning and frustrating.
This failure in the core customer service/financial process is a significant flaw that needs immediate attention. While I appreciate the ease of ordering, I cannot continue to use an app that processes a refund request but does not actually return the money. Future users should be aware that if an issue arises and a refund is necessary, you may be left empty-handed.
I truly hope the developers fix this severe financial and customer service failure so I can resume using and recommending this app. Until the promised funds are returned, I cannot recommend it.

reviews.title: Poor service, glitchy and hard to search
reviews.text:
Customer service is useless. You spend an hour in chat just for them to escalate it (chat reps don’t have power to do anything). Half the time you get a generic irrelevant response in the escalation email and have to start all over or just give up (and be out the money for the damaged or incorrect item). Even with a few non-refunded products, it’s still cheaper overall than purchasing elsewhere. The prices are usually great especially with coupons. Just make sure to comparison shop between vendors to get the best deal! 

 The games glitch a lot and they keep adding new ones instead of fixing the existing ones! The games are just to increase your time in the app, so I don’t think they care that much. It’s something mindless to do without needing to download another app so I play anyways. The coupons you can get from playing games are sometimes helpful!  However, lately some are impossible to redeem (sell out daily within seconds).  It used to feel more worth it to play the games because you got discounts and now I only play when bored.  Too many of the games have times tasks in them or tasks that require you to make shortcuts (more phone memory) and no way around that!

The search feature is fairly useless even when searching using a photo of the item. There are so many products that exist on aliexpress, but you have to browse and search a lot to find them. reviews.title: The worst return policy of any marketplace I know.
reviews.text: I used to use this app a lot, but it looks like I’ll stop ordering anything through this application and marketplace because the return policy is extremely unfair. When you place an order, it says you have 15 days for a free return if you don’t like the item. But that’s not true. When you request a return label, they usually charge you a $7.99 shipping fee. That’s the first issue. Secondly, there’s no such thing as simply selecting a reason like “I don’t like it,” “it doesn’t fit,” “too small/too big,” and getting a return label right away. No. It takes a lot of time because AliExpress has this policy where they mark your return as “unsuccessful” and say they “need more evidence.” And unless you take photos or record a video of yourself wearing the item that doesn’t fit and upload it, they will not send you a return label. This process is extremely frustrating and time-consuming in a world where you have a family, a job, a business, and an overwhelming flow of information. Doing all these extra steps feels like a lack of respect for their customers. And since AliExpress doesn’t respect its customers, I, as a customer, prefer not to use this platform anymore, especially when there are already dozens of other platforms where you can find good, high-quality, and affordable items.
